collection.description: A gardener wonders whether distant societies could change forests, air and seas so much that the weather changes.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A gardener wonders whether distant societies could change forests, air, and seas so profoundly that grandchildren inherit different weather.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: Researchers separate ordinary seasonal variation from long-term changes they would need many observations to establish.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: A child asks how anyone can measure changes across lifetimes.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: The council debates duties to people not yet born.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: A fisherman asks how poorer communities could adapt if they caused little of the damage.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: Villagers discuss planting, protecting watersheds, and learning from mistakes at home.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: An elder warns that not every damaged ecosystem can be quickly restored.
